children.text: An atomic probe microscope measures the vertical displacement \(z\) of a cantilever by reflecting a laser onto a photodetector. The cantilever obeys \(m\ddot z+b\dot z+kz=F\), with \(k=m\omega_0^2\) and weak damping \(0<b/m\ll\omega_0\). A piezoelectric tube supplies F. A lock-in amplifier multiplies its input by the reference \(V_R=V_{R0}\sin\omega t\), then retains only the dc component. A phase shifter and photodetector complete the measurement circuit as shown. Throughout, the source calls \(\omega=\omega_0\) resonance, appropriate in the stated weak-damping limit.

nodes.alt: Original atomic probe microscope, photodetector, phase shifter, piezotube and lock-in circuit with labelled reference signals.

children.text: For \(F=F_0\sin\omega t\), write \(z=A\sin(\omega t-\phi)\), with \(A>0\), \(0\le\phi\le\pi\). Find A.
Find \(\tan\phi\), state the phase quadrant, and give A and phi at \(\omega=\omega_0\).
The input is \(V_i=V_{i0}\sin(\omega_it-\phi_i)\), with all listed constants positive. What frequency condition is necessary for a nonzero dc output? State the additional phase condition.
At the matching frequency, find the magnitude of the dc output.

The phase shifter changes the reference to \(V_R^{\prime}=V_{R0}\sin(\omega t+\pi/2)\). The piezotube produces \(F=c_1V_R^{\prime}\), and the detector produces \(V_i=c_2z\). Find the dc output magnitude at \(\omega_0\), taking \(c_1,c_2>0\).

A small mass change shifts natural frequency by \(\Delta\omega_0\), producing phase change \(\Delta\phi=\pi/1800\) at the original drive frequency. Find the mass change for \(m=1.0\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(k=1.0\,\mathrm{N/m}\), \(b/m=1.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). You may use first-order binomial and tangent expansions.
A sample exerts additional force \(f(h)\), where h is tip-sample separation. Near equilibrium \(h_0\), write \(f(h)=f(h_0)+c_3(h-h_0)\). Find the new natural frequency.

A tip with charge \(Q=6e\) passes over a trapped electron of charge \(q=e\), where \(e=-1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\). The maximum small positive shift \(\Delta\omega_0\) occurs directly over the electron. Find tip-electron distance \(d_0\), ignoring polarization and using Coulomb constant \(k_e\).
Evaluate the distance in nm for \(\Delta\omega_0=20\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), \(m=10^{-12}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(k=1.0\,\mathrm{N/m}\), \(k_e=9.0\times10^9\,\mathrm{N\,m^2/C^2}\).

statement.text:
Atomic Probe Microscope
An atomic probe microscope measures the vertical displacement \(z\) of a cantilever by reflecting a laser onto a photodetector. The cantilever obeys \(m\ddot z+b\dot z+kz=F\), with \(k=m\omega_0^2\) and weak damping \(0<b/m\ll\omega_0\). A piezoelectric tube supplies F. A lock-in amplifier multiplies its input by the reference \(V_R=V_{R0}\sin\omega t\), then retains only the dc component. A phase shifter and photodetector complete the measurement circuit as shown. Throughout, the source calls \(\omega=\omega_0\) resonance, appropriate in the stated weak-damping limit.

a.amplitude. Displacement amplitude
For \(F=F_0\sin\omega t\), write \(z=A\sin(\omega t-\phi)\), with \(A>0\), \(0\le\phi\le\pi\). Find A.
a.phase. Phase relation
Find \(\tan\phi\), state the phase quadrant, and give A and phi at \(\omega=\omega_0\).
b.frequency. Lock-in frequency condition
The input is \(V_i=V_{i0}\sin(\omega_it-\phi_i)\), with all listed constants positive. What frequency condition is necessary for a nonzero dc output? State the additional phase condition.
b.output. Lock-in output magnitude
At the matching frequency, find the magnitude of the dc output.
c. Phase-shifted microscope signal
The phase shifter changes the reference to \(V_R^{\prime}=V_{R0}\sin(\omega t+\pi/2)\). The piezotube produces \(F=c_1V_R^{\prime}\), and the detector produces \(V_i=c_2z\). Find the dc output magnitude at \(\omega_0\), taking \(c_1,c_2>0\).
d. Detectable mass change
A small mass change shifts natural frequency by \(\Delta\omega_0\), producing phase change \(\Delta\phi=\pi/1800\) at the original drive frequency. Find the mass change for \(m=1.0\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(k=1.0\,\mathrm{N/m}\), \(b/m=1.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). You may use first-order binomial and tangent expansions.
e. Force-gradient frequency
A sample exerts additional force \(f(h)\), where h is tip-sample separation. Near equilibrium \(h_0\), write \(f(h)=f(h_0)+c_3(h-h_0)\). Find the new natural frequency.
f.formula. Trapped-charge depth
A tip with charge \(Q=6e\) passes over a trapped electron of charge \(q=e\), where \(e=-1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\). The maximum small positive shift \(\Delta\omega_0\) occurs directly over the electron. Find tip-electron distance \(d_0\), ignoring polarization and using Coulomb constant \(k_e\).
f.value. Charge depth value
Evaluate the distance in nm for \(\Delta\omega_0=20\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), \(m=10^{-12}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(k=1.0\,\mathrm{N/m}\), \(k_e=9.0\times10^9\,\mathrm{N\,m^2/C^2}\).

children.text: Equating sine and cosine coefficients after substitution gives \[A=\frac{F_0}{\sqrt{m^2(\omega_0^2-\omega^2)^2+b^2\omega^2}}.\]

\[\tan\phi=\frac{b\omega}{m(\omega_0^2-\omega^2)}.\] The phase is below \(\pi/2\) for \(\omega<\omega_0\), and above it for \(\omega>\omega_0\). At \(\omega_0\), \(A=F_0/(b\omega_0)\) and \(\phi=\pi/2\). The exact amplitude maximum is at \(\sqrt{\omega_0^2-b^2/(2m^2)}\), whose weak-damping difference from \(\omega_0\) is neglected in the source.
Product-to-sum gives a difference-frequency term and a sum-frequency term. A dc term is possible only if \(\omega=\omega_i\). It is nonzero only when \(\cos\phi_i\ne0\).
The signed dc component is \(V_{i0}V_{R0}\cos\phi_i/2\), so its magnitude is \(V_{i0}V_{R0}|\cos\phi_i|/2\). The absolute value is required when the question asks for magnitude.

The cantilever lags its drive by \(\pi/2\), cancelling the phase-shifter advance. Thus the detector signal is in phase with the original reference. Its amplitude is \(c_1c_2V_{R0}/(b\omega_0)\), giving \[V_{dc}=\frac{c_1c_2V_{R0}^2}{2b\omega_0}.\]

With fixed k, \(\Delta\omega_0=-\omega_0\Delta m/(2m)\). Linearizing the phase at fixed drive gives \(\Delta\phi=-2m\Delta\omega_0/b\). Thus \[\Delta m=(b/\omega_0)\Delta\phi=1.7\times10^{-18}\,\mathrm{kg}.\] The rendered source gives \(k=1.0\,\mathrm{N/m}\), not the 0.1 produced by its faulty text extraction.
The constant force moves the equilibrium, while the gradient changes stiffness to \(k-c_3\). Thus \[\omega_0^{\prime}=\sqrt{\omega_0^2-c_3/m},\] assuming \(k-c_3>0\).
Directly over the charge, \(f=k_eqQ/h^2\), so \(c_3=-2k_eqQ/d_0^3\). To first order \(\Delta\omega_0=-c_3/(2m\omega_0)\), giving \[d_0=\left(\frac{k_eqQ}{m\omega_0\Delta\omega_0}\right)^{1/3}.\]

solution.text:
Atomic Probe Microscope
a.amplitude. Displacement amplitude
Equating sine and cosine coefficients after substitution gives \[A=\frac{F_0}{\sqrt{m^2(\omega_0^2-\omega^2)^2+b^2\omega^2}}.\]
a.phase. Phase relation
\[\tan\phi=\frac{b\omega}{m(\omega_0^2-\omega^2)}.\] The phase is below \(\pi/2\) for \(\omega<\omega_0\), and above it for \(\omega>\omega_0\). At \(\omega_0\), \(A=F_0/(b\omega_0)\) and \(\phi=\pi/2\). The exact amplitude maximum is at \(\sqrt{\omega_0^2-b^2/(2m^2)}\), whose weak-damping difference from \(\omega_0\) is neglected in the source.
b.frequency. Lock-in frequency condition
Product-to-sum gives a difference-frequency term and a sum-frequency term. A dc term is possible only if \(\omega=\omega_i\). It is nonzero only when \(\cos\phi_i\ne0\).
b.output. Lock-in output magnitude
The signed dc component is \(V_{i0}V_{R0}\cos\phi_i/2\), so its magnitude is \(V_{i0}V_{R0}|\cos\phi_i|/2\). The absolute value is required when the question asks for magnitude.
c. Phase-shifted microscope signal
The cantilever lags its drive by \(\pi/2\), cancelling the phase-shifter advance. Thus the detector signal is in phase with the original reference. Its amplitude is \(c_1c_2V_{R0}/(b\omega_0)\), giving \[V_{dc}=\frac{c_1c_2V_{R0}^2}{2b\omega_0}.\]
d. Detectable mass change
With fixed k, \(\Delta\omega_0=-\omega_0\Delta m/(2m)\). Linearizing the phase at fixed drive gives \(\Delta\phi=-2m\Delta\omega_0/b\). Thus \[\Delta m=(b/\omega_0)\Delta\phi=1.7\times10^{-18}\,\mathrm{kg}.\] The rendered source gives \(k=1.0\,\mathrm{N/m}\), not the 0.1 produced by its faulty text extraction.
e. Force-gradient frequency
The constant force moves the equilibrium, while the gradient changes stiffness to \(k-c_3\). Thus \[\omega_0^{\prime}=\sqrt{\omega_0^2-c_3/m},\] assuming \(k-c_3>0\).
f.formula. Trapped-charge depth
Directly over the charge, \(f=k_eqQ/h^2\), so \(c_3=-2k_eqQ/d_0^3\). To first order \(\Delta\omega_0=-c_3/(2m\omega_0)\), giving \[d_0=\left(\frac{k_eqQ}{m\omega_0\Delta\omega_0}\right)^{1/3}.\]
f.value. Charge depth value
\(\omega_0=10^6\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), giving \(d_0=41\,\mathrm{nm}\).
